trustAppModal.title: Trust “{{app}}” to run its own code?
trustAppModal.scope: This applies to “{{app}}” only. Every other third-party app stays blocked.
trustAppModal.on_cancel: “Cancel” changes nothing: “{{app}}” stays in place, switched off, and you can turn it on later.
trustAppModal.on_cancel_granted: “Cancel” keeps “{{app}}” trusted and switched off; you can turn it on later from its page.
trustAppModal.on_close_desktop_unsupported: No trust decision is needed here: “{{app}}” was not installed and nothing was changed, so closing leaves nothing behind.
trustAppModal.intro: If you trust “{{app}}”, {{productName}} will allow it to do all of the following.
trustAppModal.capability_python: Run its own code inside {{productName}}, with the same access {{productName}} has — your files, your saved credentials, and the internet
trustAppModal.capability_backend: Keep a program of its own running on this computer, in the background, while {{productName}} is open
trustAppModal.capability_shell: Run commands on this computer, from a list the app ships with that you have not seen
trustAppModal.capability_note: Trusting the app grants all three, whether or not it uses them all. {{productName}} cannot limit it to less.
trustAppModal.session_approval_heading: This app also asks to control your chats
trustAppModal.session_approval_desc: Sending messages or choosing response options in your chats, approving or denying tool prompts, and switching a chat's approval mode.
trustAppModal.session_approval_modes: Chat approval modes it can set
trustAppModal.revocable: You can take this back at any time in Settings → Security → Third-party apps. The app stops working when you do.
trustAppModal.not_reviewed: {{productName}} lists this app but has not reviewed its code, and the name above comes from the app itself.
trustAppModal.registry_community: A community registry listed “{{app}}”. Its contributors check listings lightly, and the {{productName}} team did not vet this listing. Trust it only if you recognise it.
trustAppModal.registry_community_credentialed: A community registry listed “{{app}}”. Its contributors check listings lightly, and the {{productName}} team did not vet this listing. {{productName}} downloads it with your saved Git sign-in, so trust it only if you recognise it.
trustAppModal.failed: Trusting “{{app}}” is what turns it on. It is now trusted, but it could not be turned on. To remove the trust, open Settings → Security → Third-party apps.
trustAppModal.failed_generic: Trusting “{{app}}” is what turns it on. It could not be turned on, and trust was not saved.
trustAppModal.install_outcome: Trusting “{{app}}” does not turn it on: it installs switched off, and you turn it on from this page when you're ready.
trustAppModal.update_outcome: Trusting “{{app}}” updates it: the new version replaces the one you have.
trustAppModal.install_on_cancel: “Cancel” changes nothing: nothing is installed, and “{{app}}” is not trusted.
trustAppModal.install_on_cancel_granted: “Cancel” keeps “{{app}}” trusted, and the install does not run again.
trustAppModal.install_failed: “{{app}}” is now trusted, but it could not be installed. To remove the trust, open Settings → Security → Third-party apps.
trustAppModal.install_failed_generic: “{{app}}” could not be installed, and trust was not saved.
trustAppModal.update_on_cancel: “Cancel” changes nothing: “{{app}}” stays as it is, on the version you have, and is not trusted.
trustAppModal.update_on_cancel_granted: “Cancel” keeps “{{app}}” trusted, and the update does not run again; the version you have stays as it is.
trustAppModal.update_failed: “{{app}}” is now trusted, but it could not be updated. To remove the trust, open Settings → Security → Third-party apps.
trustAppModal.update_failed_generic: “{{app}}” could not be updated, and trust was not saved.
trustAppModal.failed_generic_next_ask: Choose “Trust and try again”. If it fails again, choose “Ask the agent” to find out why.
trustAppModal.failed_generic_next_offline: {{productName}} is not connected right now, so “Trust and try again” stays off until it reconnects.
trustAppModal.failed_desktop_unsupported: “{{app}}” can't be installed in the desktop version of {{productName}}, and nothing was changed.
trustAppModal.failed_desktop_unsupported_help: It needs Python packages the desktop build can't add; ask the app's author to ship them with the app, or open {{productName}} in a web browser instead of the desktop version.

jobForm.minimal_context_description: Run with a fresh, empty context: skips your saved context (memory, lessons, steering and skills) and prior session history. Leave off if the job refers to things you've told the agent before, or drives a skill.

jobForm.mode_advice_script: This job reads like a mechanical check that needs no reasoning at all. The cheapest form is a script job, which takes no agent turn — in the Chat tab, ask to create a script job that does this. Minimal context is the next best thing here.
jobForm.chat_folder_description: Put this job's chat tab under a folder in the chat sidebar, so its runs are easy to find together. Filing does not hide anything: notifications and Slack delivery are unchanged.
jobForm.chat_folder_hidden_in_chat: Turn off “Hide in chat” to use this. A hidden job's runs get no chat session, so there is nothing to file. The folder you pick is kept.
jobForm.chat_folder_needs_persistent_session: Filing runs into a folder needs a persistent session. This job was created to start a fresh session every run, so there is no tab to file. That choice is made when a job is created, not on this form.

jobForm.chat_folder_none_yet: No folders yet. Save this job now; create a folder in the chat sidebar, then reopen the job to pick it.
jobForm.chat_folder_was_deleted: The folder this job filed into was deleted. Pick another, or save to leave runs unfiled.
jobForm.auto_pause_after_failures: Auto-pause after N failures in a row
jobForm.auto_pause_after_failures_description: 0 means never pause. From the 5th failure in a row, a job set to 0 or above 5 waits 5 minutes before its next run, doubling up to an hour.
jobForm.auto_pause_after_failures_invalid: The auto-pause limit must be a whole number from 0 to 10000.

kiroPrerequisiteGate.another_sandbox_already_confines_kiro_cr: Another sandbox already confines {{productName}}, so its own sandbox cannot nest inside it. This host's sandbox is not broken.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.copy_failed: Copy failed. Select the command text and copy it manually.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.if_you_are_diagnosing_this_from_a_termin: If you are diagnosing this from a terminal, note that kiro-cli diagnostic reports nothing until the Kiro CLI app itself is running — launch it with kiro-cli launch first. That refusal is not the cause of this.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.kiro_cli_is_installed_but_could_not_be_v: Kiro CLI is installed but could not be verified
kiroPrerequisiteGate.kiro_cli_is_installed_but_too_old: Kiro CLI is installed, but this version predates the acp command {{productName}} launches every session through. Update it and this page continues on its own.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.kiro_cli_is_installed_finish_signing_in_: Kiro CLI is installed. Finish signing in to continue.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.kiro_cli_will_not_load_kiro_crew_s_agent: Kiro CLI will not load {{productName}}'s agent specs
kiroPrerequisiteGate.kiro_crew_installs_the_agent_specs_kiro_: {{productName}} installs the agent specs Kiro CLI loads before it can answer anything.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.kiro_crew_isolates_the_agent_in_an_os_le: {{productName}} isolates the agent in an OS-level sandbox before it runs anything.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.kiro_crew_writes_its_own_agent_specs_whe: {{productName}} writes its own agent specs where Kiro CLI reads them. Without them Kiro CLI cannot resolve the agent, so every message fails. Check again rewrites the specs and reports what went wrong.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.remedy_apparmor_service_install: Install {{productName}} as a service. It also writes a narrow AppArmor profile (kirocrew-userns) that grants only the user-namespace permission, to the {{productName}} service alone — nothing else on the machine is loosened.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.remedy_max_user_namespaces: User namespace creation hit the per-user cap, which usually means user.max_user_namespaces is 0 on a hardened host. Raise it, and persist the value in /etc/sysctl.d/ so it survives a reboot.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.remedy_mount_denied: Run the container with AppArmor unconfined and a seccomp profile that permits unshare and mount (the Linux sandbox guide below provides kirocrew-seccomp.json); no root is needed. If the pod policy cannot change, set agent.sandbox_allow_unsandboxed_exec=true in config.json.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.remedy_no_user_ns: This kernel was built without user-namespace support (CONFIG_USER_NS), so there is no setting to change. A different kernel is the only fix.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.remedy_spec_rejected_rewrite: Rewrite the specs from scratch on the gateway host. This discards {{productName}}'s own MCP tool selections and rebuilds them from defaults.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.remedy_spec_rejected_update: Update {{productName}}. This is the fix when Kiro CLI has moved to a spec format this version does not know how to write.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.remedy_userns_denied: The kernel refused to create the user namespace. On Debian-family hosts check this legacy knob, and persist the value in /etc/sysctl.d/ so it survives a reboot. Inside a container it is usually the container's own seccomp filter denying unshare, which is fixed with container run flags rather than host settings.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.repair_rewrites_the_specs_kiro_crew_owns: Check again asks Kiro CLI to load the specs again. It does not rewrite them, because overwriting a spec that is already on disk would discard any MCP tool access you have changed. If re-checking does not clear this, one of the two remedies below will.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.run_kirocrew_doctor_on_the_gateway_host_: Run this on the gateway host for a full prerequisite report, including which sandbox step failed.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.enterprise_start_url_hint: Enter it first: the command below fills it in, then you can copy it. It is your AWS access portal address; your IT team has it.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.enterprise_sign_in_aside: Sign this gateway in to your organization's account once, and {{productName}} will take it from here.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.relock_ask_owner: Ask the {{productName}} owner to sign this gateway in again. This notice clears once they do.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.relock_enterprise_new_window: To sign in again, open the dashboard in a new window or tab. Its sign-in screen shows the command with a copy button. This window keeps your work.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.relock_exact_command_hint: This gateway uses its own copy of Kiro CLI. To sign in again, open the dashboard in a new window or tab: its sign-in screen shows the exact command with a copy button. This window keeps your work.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.relock_run_in_terminal: Run this in a terminal to sign in again. This notice clears once you do.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.sign_in_bundled_hint: The long path is the desktop app's own copy of Kiro CLI ({{binary}}). Run one of these commands exactly as shown.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.sign_in_bundled_hint_windows: The long first part starts PowerShell and runs the desktop app's own copy of Kiro CLI ({{binary}}) with its self-update turned off. Run one of these commands exactly as shown, in PowerShell or Command Prompt.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.sign_in_method_note: Both open a browser to finish signing in. Pick the one that matches your plan — the sign-in page offers a personal Builder ID alongside organization SSO, and a Builder ID carries a smaller set of models.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.sign_in_personal_label: Personal account — Builder ID, Google, or GitHub
kiroPrerequisiteGate.sign_in_sso_hint: Prompts for your organization's start URL and region.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.sign_in_with_kiro_cli_on_the_gateway_hos: Sign in with Kiro CLI on the gateway host, then check again. Kiro CLI manages the sign-in and keeps the credentials.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.the_check_hit_a_temporary_limit_and_was_: The check hit a temporary resource limit. Try again — do not disable the sandbox.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.the_files_are_on_disk_but_kiro_cli_refus: The files are on disk, but Kiro CLI refuses them, so it drops them from its agent list. {{productName}}'s agent then resolves to Kiro CLI's default one, without any of {{productName}}'s tools.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.the_gateway_returned_an_unexpected_error: The gateway returned an unexpected error.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.the_gateway_returned_no_prerequisite_sta: The gateway returned no prerequisite status.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.this_container_grants_namespaces_but_ref: This container grants the user and mount namespaces, but its runtime policy refused the mount that makes them private, as a container runtime's default AppArmor profile does on Kubernetes nodes. {{productName}} stays blocked until that policy is relaxed or you explicitly accept running the agent with your credentials exposed.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.this_host_allows_user_namespaces_but_the: This host allows user namespaces, but the kernel then denied the mount namespace — the signature of Ubuntu 23.10 and newer, which moves any process that creates a user namespace into a restricted AppArmor profile. {{productName}} refuses to run the agent unisolated rather than expose your credentials, so it stays blocked until the profile is in place.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.this_host_provides_no_os_level_sandbox_s: This host provides no OS-level sandbox, so {{productName}} cannot isolate the agent. It refuses to run the agent unsandboxed rather than expose your credentials.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.this_kiro_cli_is_too_old_for_the_acp_com: This Kiro CLI is too old for the acp command {{productName}} needs. Update it here.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.this_page_detects_kiro_cli_automatically: Leave this page open. It checks the gateway host and continues on its own once Kiro CLI is installed.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.update_kiro_cli_runs_on_host: Runs <0>{{command}}</0> on the gateway host for you.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.your_kiro_cli_is_out_of_date: Your Kiro CLI is out of date
kiroPrerequisiteGate.attempt_failed_remedy: Fix the cause named above (often a permissions or install problem), then press {{action}} to try again. If it keeps failing, reinstall Kiro CLI.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.kiro_cli_is_not_installed_yet: Kiro CLI is the default agent and isn't installed on this host yet.

kiroPrerequisiteGate.unzip_missing_install_first: First, install unzip. The installer needs it, and the gateway host does not have it. Use one of these commands or your system's package manager.
kiroPrerequisiteGate.install_kiro_cli_then_run_on_host: Then run this on the {{platform}} gateway host to install Kiro CLI.

devFleetPage.stages_the_code_behind_the_live_dashboar: Stages this worktree as the live target (same port, same data). Dev Fleet cannot restart this gateway, so the swap takes effect when you run `{{cmd}}` yourself — this page will NOT reconnect on its own. Refused unless the worktree is provisioned and built.
devFleetPage.keeps_name_the_live_target_and_discards_: Keeps “{{name}}” as the live target and discards the staged switch to “{{staged}}”. Nothing restarts — the gateway keeps running the code it is running now.
devFleetPage.keeps_this_checkout_the_live_target_and_: Keeps this checkout the live target and discards the staged switch to “{{staged}}” (nothing restarts)
devFleetPage.cutover_staged_run_cmd_to_finish_or_canc: Cutover staged: this worktree becomes live when the gateway next starts. Run `{{cmd}}` to finish it, or use this row’s menu → Cancel staged cutover to back out. The gateway is still running the previous checkout until then.
devFleetPage.keeps_the_live_checkout_the_live_target_: Keeps the live checkout as the live target and discards the staged switch to {{staged}} (nothing restarts)
devFleetPage.restarting_completes_the_pending_cutover: Restarting completes the pending cutover: the gateway comes back up on "{{staged}}", not the current checkout. The dashboard will briefly disconnect and reconnect automatically. To back out instead, use Cancel staged cutover.
devFleetPage.no_checkout_found_help: Dev Fleet manages the git worktrees of a {{productName}} source checkout. None was found in your project directory, in the checkout serving this dashboard, or in the usual clone locations.
devFleetPage.no_checkout_found_action: Add dev_fleet.repo_path to config.json in your {{productName}} data directory (~/.kiro/crew by default), and this page picks it up on its next refresh. The environment variable below works too, but a running gateway cannot see a variable set after it started, so that route needs a restart.

hooksPage.hooks_run_shell_commands_on_chat_events_: Hooks run shell commands on chat events: AgentSpawn, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop. Tool hooks support matcher patterns to filter by tool name. A row marked not fired yet is supported by the agent but nothing here fires it yet; one marked never fires is not supported at all. Test runs either one now.
hooksPage.read_only_view_of_provider_hooks: Read-only view of provider hooks from {{path}}. These fire on tool calls including auto-approved ones.
hooksPage.script_hooks_fire_shell_commands_on_chat: Script hooks fire shell commands on chat lifecycle events. PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks can filter by tool name pattern. Choosing a marked trigger shows what its mark means, and Test runs the hook either way.
hooksPage.runs_on_no_event_yet: The agent supports this trigger, but nothing here fires it yet. Test runs it now.
hooksPage.runs_only_via_test: This trigger never fires on its own. Only Test runs it.
hooksPage.unsent_reason_trigger: Not sent to kiro-cli: kiro-cli has no event for this trigger. It can run on PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart, Stop.
hooksPage.unsent_reason_agent_action: Not sent to kiro-cli: kiro-cli runs commands only, not an agent action's prompt.
hooksPage.unsent_reason_disabled: Not sent to kiro-cli: it is set to "enabled": false. Its script in ~/.kiro/hooks is skipped too.
hooksPage.unsent_reason_confirm: Not sent to kiro-cli: "confirm": true asks for a prompt kiro-cli cannot show. Remove it to run the hook. Its script in ~/.kiro/hooks is skipped too.
hooksPage.failed_to_load_unsent: Couldn't check which hooks were not sent to kiro-cli
hooksPage.skills_inert_warning: These skills can't fire on this configuration: {{skills}}. To save, switch to UserPromptSubmit or AgentSpawn without a command — or remove the skills.
hooksPage.saved_switched_off: This hook will be saved turned off — nothing fires this trigger yet.
hooksPage.no_matcher_for_trigger: No matcher: this trigger has no event data to filter.
hooksPage.saved_switched_off_never: This hook will be saved turned off — this trigger never fires on its own.
hooksPage.on_but_nothing_fires: On, but nothing fires this trigger yet.
hooksPage.skills_only_for_prompt_hooks: Skills load only on UserPromptSubmit or AgentSpawn hooks that run no command.
hooksPage.on_but_never_fires: On, but this trigger never fires on its own.

settings.title: Ingestion Settings
settings.description: Changes apply on the next watcher sweep.
settings.embed_rate_desc: How many embedding requests per minute when indexing documents into the vector store. Lower values reduce system load but slow down indexing. 0 = unlimited.
settings.model_desc: LLM used for chunking & extracting document content. "Auto" inherits your default chat model. Pick a smaller, cheaper model from the list to control extraction cost.
settings.pool_size_desc: Concurrent extraction workers. More workers = faster indexing, higher peak resource usage.
settings.auto_add_desc: Let the agent add documents it reads during normal work to the Knowledge Library.
settings.auto_artifacts_desc: Mirror documents you save as artifacts into the Knowledge Library.
settings.effort_hint: Default runs High effort until you pick a level.
settings.effort_model_unknown_hint: The model is picked at run time, so effort applies only when the resolved model supports it. Default runs High effort.

assessment.how_measured: A server reads as not measured until {{productName}} probes it. The button below measures every unmeasured server at once; the MCP server list under {{link}} also probes a couple at a time when it is refreshed.
assessment.lede: What {{productName}} managed to observe about each server, and how that lines up with what the server is running as right now. Nothing on this view changes anything — the switches live under Servers.
assessment.measure_failed: The measurement pass stopped early; see the gateway log
assessment.reason_handshake_not_reproducible: Did not replay the same handshake when started twice; this may come from the caller or from the server's own startup. Measuring again retests it
assessment.reason_declares_caller_identity: Declares that it can tell its callers apart
assessment.reason_session_bound_by_construction: Works out which session is calling from its own process, so a shared backend cannot tell one session's data from another's
assessment.reason_no_objection_found: Nothing disqualifying was found, which is weaker than evidence that sharing is safe
assessment.reason_no_tool_annotations: No tool declared whether it only reads
assessment.reason_not_probed: Never measured, so nothing is claimed either way
assessment.reason_not_stdio: Not a stdio server, so it cannot be shared
assessment.reason_observed_hazard: Already seen behaving differently per caller while shared
assessment.reason_degrades_when_shared: Advertises a capability that loses function on a shared backend, without putting anything at risk
assessment.reason_preflight_not_run: Declares it, but has not been measured yet
assessment.reason_preflight_passed: Measured under two different callers and answered the same way
assessment.reason_rotating_secret_env: A shared backend never receives this credential, so if the server authenticates with it, sharing fails at startup
assessment.shared_without_support: Backend sharing is already in effect for servers whose evidence argues against it. Servers affected: {{count}}
assessment.measure_progress_failed: Could not read the measurement progress.
assessment.legend: Recommending a shared backend takes the server saying it can tell its callers apart, and few servers say it. A measurement rules out a per-caller handshake but cannot see state a tool call would create, so most healthy servers rest at measured or no objection found — the conservative answer, not a missing one, and sharing remains your call.

agentCfgTab.agent_config_tip: The {{process}} agent definition — prompt, tools, MCP servers, model settings. This is the execution layer config, separate from {{productName}}'s operational bindings.

kiroCrewCfgTab.ceiling_on_the_auto_sized_concurrent_sub: Ceiling on the auto-sized concurrent subagent count (only applies when Max Concurrent Subagents = 0). The host memory/CPU formula never exceeds this. Range 3–64. Default: 32.
kiroCrewCfgTab.controls_how_many_subagents_can_run_conc: Controls how many subagents can run concurrently and how many tool calls each subagent is allowed. Changes take effect on the next subagent spawn.
kiroCrewCfgTab.maximum_subagents_running_at_once: Maximum subagents running at once. 0 = auto-size from host memory/CPU (capped at {{cap}}). A fixed value must be 3 or more (up to {{cap}}). Default: 0 (auto).
kiroCrewCfgTab.named_agent_definitions: Named mates that bind a custom agent, workspace, and memory store together. Edit config.json to add or modify mates.
kiroCrewCfgTab.named_memory_stores_with_optional_per_st: Named memory stores with optional per-store embedding overrides. Unset fields inherit from the top-level memory section.
kiroCrewCfgTab.named_workspace_directories_each_agent_b: Named workspace directories. Each agent binds to one workspace.
kiroCrewCfgTab.subagent_save_note: Helpers an agent starts for side tasks. Changes apply when you press Save.
kiroCrewCfgTab.tool_call_budget_per_subagent_1_1000_def: How many tool calls one subagent may make before it stops. A turn is one tool call (1–1000). Default: 1000.
kiroCrewCfgTab.max_age_for_pooled_processes_0_disables_: Restart a waiting agent after this many seconds. 0 keeps it until a chat uses it.
kiroCrewCfgTab.number_of_pre_spawned_processes_0_disabl: How many agents to keep started and waiting. 0 turns this off.
kiroCrewCfgTab.agent_for_pool_processes_empty_uses_defa: Which mate the waiting agents start as. Empty uses the default mate.
kiroCrewCfgTab.warm_pool_description: Keep a few agents started in the background, so a new chat opens right away.
kiroCrewCfgTab.warm_pool_save_note: Keeps agents started so new chats open at once. Changes save right away, and you can change them back.

mcpTab.outdated_help: No probe result from the last 30 minutes. Select the refresh button (↻, top right) to check it again.
mcpTab.routed_help: The MCP gateway starts this server and resolves its secret:// reference, so the dashboard does not probe it and this badge makes no health claim. Each chat session reports its own servers in its MCP panel.
mcpTab.not_probed_routing_guide: How to route this server through the MCP gateway

mcpTab.sign_in_required_help: This server uses OAuth and nobody has signed in yet. <chatLink>Go to chat</chatLink>, start a new session, and send any message — you'll be asked to approve the sign-in in chat. Then probe to refresh this list.

mcpTab.sign_in_required_next: Once you have approved it, use the Probe MCP servers button above this table; this row will then read Signed in.

crewmatesSection.description: Server settings for mates, not previews. They're saved on the server, so they apply on every device.
crewmatesSection.reply_threads: Reply threads on mate chat messages
crewmatesSection.reply_threads_desc: Let any message in a mate's chat carry its own reply thread, opened in the side panel while the chat stays visible. Off, the Reply in thread control is not offered and existing threads are hidden, not deleted.
crewmatesSection.failed_to_save: Couldn't save the mate setting. Try again.

developerPanel.feature_previews_desc: Unreleased features and pages. Your choices here are saved on this {{productName}}, so they apply wherever you open the dashboard, in any browser or in the desktop app. The pages stay hidden from the sidebar and from Search Everywhere until you turn them on here; the switches themselves do show up in Settings search. Unpolished on purpose.
developerPanel.feature_previews_save_denied: Only the owner of this {{productName}} can change feature previews, so “{{name}}” was switched back.
developerPanel.feature_previews_save_failed: Couldn’t save “{{name}}”, so it was switched back. Try again.
developerPanel.feature_previews_carry_failed: “{{name}}” is on in this browser only: it couldn’t be saved on this {{productName}}. Reload the page to try again; it stays on until then.
developerPanel.feature_previews_carry_denied: “{{name}}” was turned on in this browser before it could be saved here. Only the owner of this {{productName}} can save it, so it stays on in this browser only.

computerUsePanel.computer_use_lets_the_agent_read_any_app: Computer use lets the agent read any app window and send clicks and keystrokes into it. Most clicks are delivered straight to the app and leave your pointer alone, but the agent can ask to move the real pointer when a target needs it. Password fields are never read; nothing else limits which apps it may drive.
computerUsePanel.computer_use_not_available: Computer use is not available on {{platform}}.
computerUsePanel.draw_a_cursor_that_glides_to_each_target: Draw a cursor that glides to each target and pulses when it clicks, so you can follow along on screen. Purely visual — it changes nothing about what the agent is allowed to do, and it only appears for clicks that move the real pointer.
computerUsePanel.how_many_controls_one_window_reading_ret: How many controls one window reading returns. A window with more than this gets truncated, and the agent is told so. Raise it for dense apps (a spreadsheet, an IDE); lower it to spend fewer tokens per reading.
computerUsePanel.how_much_of_a_window_the_agent_reads_at_: How much of a window the agent reads at once. These are cost and speed dials, not security settings — every value stays within a built-in ceiling. Leave them alone unless a window is too large to read in one pass, or screenshots feel slow.
computerUsePanel.longest_edge_of_the_screenshot_in_pixels: Longest edge of the screenshot, in pixels. Smaller is cheaper and faster to read; larger keeps small text legible if the agent has to fall back to the image.
computerUsePanel.not_detected_does_not_always_mean_unavai: Not detected does not always mean unavailable — macOS attributes a permission grant to the process that launched {{productName}}, not to {{productName}} itself.
computerUsePanel.on_windows_keystrokes_take_your_keyboard: On Windows, keystrokes take your keyboard focus and coordinate clicks move your real cursor — there is no per-app input route on this platform.
computerUsePanel.the_app_lists_in_computer_use_json_could: The app lists in computer_use.json could not be read, so they are shown empty here. The agent still refuses every action that depends on them until the file is valid JSON.
computerUsePanel.your_chat_sessions_were_restarted_so_thi: Your chat sessions were restarted so this takes effect right away — Kiro reads its tool list once per session, so an open chat would not have picked it up otherwise. Your messages are still there; the agent re-reads its context on your next message.
computerUsePanel.your_chat_sessions_were_restarted: Your chat sessions were restarted. Your messages are still there.

slackPanel.auto_link_sessions: Connect new sessions to Slack automatically
slackPanel.auto_link_sessions_desc: Every new dashboard session gets a Slack thread on its first message, in your private direct message with the bot. Sessions started by cron, apps or sub-agents, sessions that began in Slack or another messaging app, and incognito or temporary sessions are left alone. A session connected this way does not count as a Slack session for the folder setting below: it stays where it is in the sidebar, and only conversations that start in Slack are filed.
slackPanel.create_the_slack_app_from_the_manifest:
Create the Slack app from the pre-filled manifest below (Socket Mode and permissions
            included, named KiroCrew-{{alias}}). Install it to your
            workspace, then paste the bot token and app-level token here.
slackPanel.save_failed_is_the_gateway_running: Save failed. Is the gateway running?
slackPanel.saved_restart_the_gateway_to_apply: Saved. Restart the gateway to apply.
slackPanel.slack_connection_failed_at_startup: Slack connection failed at startup ({{error}}). Check network access to slack.com, then restart the gateway.
slackPanel.slack_rejected_the_stored_tokens_invalid: Slack rejected the stored tokens (invalid_auth). Replace them below, then restart the gateway.
slackPanel.tokens_are_saved_but_not_yet_active_rest: Tokens are saved but not yet active. Restart the gateway to connect.
slackPanel.verified_with_slack_and_saved_restart_th: Verified with Slack and saved. Restart the gateway to connect.

slackPanel.where_to_find_the_bot_token: Where to find the bot token

slackCode.intro: Run your coding work natively in Slack. Agent sessions give every thread a live status and a Stop button. Turning a switch on needs a few more permissions for your Slack app, which you add with the steps below.
slackCode.agent_sessions_desc: Slack threads show a live status and title, and a Stop button that stops the agent's current reply.
slackCode.agent_sessions_manifest_warning: Agent sessions: saving this manifest in Slack can't be undone. Slack moves your app's conversations from its separate Chat and History tabs into the app's Messages tab, where each thread shows a live status and a Stop button. DMs and channel threads keep working, and turning Agent sessions off here does not switch the app back.
slackCode.agent_sessions_note: Turning this on changes nothing in Slack yet. It only adds to the app manifest, the setup text you copy into Slack in the steps below.
slackCode.update_keeps_working: Slack keeps working as before until you update.
slackCode.detail_up_to_date: Your installed app has every permission these switches need.
slackCode.detail_needs_update: Your installed app is missing permissions these switches need. Update the manifest and reinstall the app.
slackCode.detail_feature_disabled: The app has the permissions, but Slack says this workspace does not have {{features}} enabled. No app update is needed: ask a Slack workspace admin to enable it, then select Check again.
slackCode.detail_unknown: Slack did not report which permissions the app holds, so {{productName}} cannot tell whether it is current.
slackCode.unknown_next: Select Check again first. If it still cannot check and threads show no Stop button, your app needs the update.
slackCode.detail_not_configured: Add a bot token above to check your installed app.
slackCode.detail_token_rejected: Slack rejected the saved bot token. Paste a current one in Slack bot token at the top of this page, then select Check again.
slackCode.detail_token_type: Slack refused this kind of token for Agent sessions. Paste the app's bot token (it starts with xoxb-, under OAuth & Permissions in your app's Slack settings) in Slack bot token at the top of this page, then select Check again.
slackCode.detail_check_failed: Slack could not be reached to check the app. Select Check again to retry.
slackCode.status_load_failed: Could not check the installed Slack app. Check again in a moment.
slackCode.pending_save: Save your Slack settings to apply these changes to the generated manifest. The lines below show what saving adds; the steps to update your Slack app appear once it is saved.
slackCode.extra_scopes: Your app still holds permissions these switches no longer need. You can remove them in Slack.
slackCode.step_paste: Open your app's App Manifest page, replace the YAML with the copied manifest and select Save Changes.
slackCode.step_reinstall: When Slack asks, reinstall the app to your workspace (Install App → Reinstall).
slackCode.step_check: Select Check again: the status reads Up to date.
slackCode.up_to_date_events: Permissions are up to date. Slack does not report event subscriptions, so if threads show no Stop button, copy the manifest and save it on the app's App Manifest page again.
slackCode.events_unverifiable: Slack reports an app's permissions but not its event subscriptions, so the status checks permissions only.
slackCode.cap_active: Slack app prepared: it has the permissions this needs.
slackCode.replace_warning: Only if you edited this app in Slack by hand: add just the lines above instead of replacing the YAML, because replacing it replaces the app's whole configuration.

botChannelPanel.configuration_is_saved_but_the_channel_i: Configuration is saved but the channel is not running. Restart the gateway to connect.

botChannelPanel.saved_restart_the_gateway_to_apply: Saved. Restart the gateway to apply.
botChannelPanel.soft_context_threshold_must_be_a_number_: Soft context threshold must be a number between 1 and 100
botChannelPanel.start_the_channel_at_gateway_startup: Start the {{channel}} channel at gateway startup (requires a bot token).
botChannelPanel.verified_with_channel_and_saved: Verified with {{channel}} and saved. Restart the gateway to connect.
botChannelPanel.where_to_find_the_bot_token: Where to find the bot token
botChannelPanel.sdk_missing_body: The {{channel}} channel needs the {{package}} package, which is not installed by default. Run the command below in a terminal to add it.
botChannelPanel.sdk_restart_after_install: Then restart the gateway to start the {{channel}} channel.

chatPanel.auto_always_visible: Always visible in chat model pickers
chatPanel.click_a_suggested_reply_to_send_it_insta: Click a suggested reply to send it instantly. {{mod}}+Click to select multiple.
chatPanel.double_click_to_edit_desc: When off, a double-click on your message selects a word as in any text.
chatPanel.scroll_on_send: Jump to the bottom when you send
chatPanel.scroll_on_send_desc: When off, sending a message leaves the transcript where it is.
chatPanel.sidebar_click_opens_tab: Open Sidebar Sessions in a Session Tab
chatPanel.sidebar_click_opens_tab_desc: A click opens the session in its own session tab instead of replacing the active tab's session.
chatPanel.copy_on_select_desc: Copy text to the clipboard as soon as you select it in the conversation with the mouse. The Quote, Ask about this and Copy row still opens.
chatPanel.maximum_characters_retained_in_the_compl: Maximum characters retained in the completion event after applying the truncation mode. 0 disables truncation entirely. Default {{n}}.
chatPanel.opt_in_split_the_chat_into_resizable_ses: Opt-in: split the chat into resizable session panes ({{mod}}+D). Experimental.
chatPanel.dim_inactive_panes_desc: In split view, fade every pane that does not have keyboard focus. When off, all panes stay at full brightness and the accent border marks the focused one.
chatPanel.selectable_models_description: Choose which advertised models appear in Chat model pickers. Auto and an active session model always remain visible.
chatPanel.role_effort_hint: Applies only on reasoning-capable models. 'Model default' applies no override — this work does not inherit your Default Reasoning Effort.
chatPanel.model_for_background_lite_heartbeat_work: Model for background work — title generation, history compaction, and heartbeat polling.
chatPanel.subagent_pin_runtime_cost: Setting Subagent Model or Subagent Effort to anything but its default runs each subagent in its own process, about 0.55 GB of memory each, which can slow a machine with 16 GB or less. With both on their defaults, subagents can share the chat's process.
chatPanel.role_model_auto_hint: 'Auto' lets the provider pick — it does not inherit your Default Model. Pin a model to run this work on it.
chatPanel.failed_to_save_chat_setting: Couldn't save this chat setting. Free up browser storage (clear site data for other tabs or apps), then try again.
chatPanel.failed_to_save_default_reasoning_effort: Failed to save default reasoning effort
chatPanel.model_default_applies_no_override_the_mo: How long models think before answering by default. 'Model default' applies no override — the model picks its own effort.
chatPanel.busy_alt_action_summary: Steer adds your message to the current turn without stopping it; Queue waits for the turn to finish.
chatPanel.busy_alt_action_desc: {{chord}} sends with the other action for one message. This is the default; chats where you already chose a mode from the send button keep that choice.
chatPanel.busy_alt_action_desc_no_chord: The one-message flip shortcut is available only when Enter sends; use the send button's menu instead. This is the default; chats where you already chose a mode from the send button keep that choice.
chatPanel.what_enter_does_while_the_agent_is_worki: What Enter does while the agent is working
chatPanel.show_occasional_feature_discovery_tips_a: Show occasional feature discovery tips above the composer while the agent is working
chatPanel.spellcheck_input_desc: Underline misspelled words in the message input with a red squiggle. Turn it off to stop the red underlines while you type.
chatPanel.inline_markdown_input_desc: Show bold, italic, strikethrough and inline code in the message input as you type. Turning it on also switches the message input to a rich-text editor that is still in beta; turn this off to go back to the plain input. The markdown markers stay visible and the message you send is unchanged.
chatPanel.show_pasted_text_in_full_desc: Keep a long paste as editable text in the message input instead of folding it into a paste chip. When this is off, {{chord}} keeps a single paste as text. A very large paste can make the input slow.
chatPanel.summarize_each_session_by_intent_in_the_: Uses tokens on turns that change the session.
chatPanel.failed_to_save_session_summaries: Failed to save session summaries setting
chatPanel.title_refresh_every_turns_desc: Default is the built-in schedule (turns 8 and 24). Each refresh uses tokens.
chatPanel.title_refresh_every_turns_hint: Re-checks an auto-generated session title at each interval of your turns and renames the session when its topic has moved. The shortest interval is 4 turns. A title you renamed yourself never changes.
chatPanel.failed_to_save_title_refresh: Failed to save title refresh setting
chatPanel.effort_needs_reasoning_model: Applies only on reasoning-capable models, so it has no effect on the model selected above.
chatPanel.effort_default_needs_reasoning_model: How long models think before answering by default. Applies only on reasoning-capable models, so it has no effect on the model selected above.
chatPanel.model_tried_when_your_current_model_stay: Model tried when your current model stays rate-limited past its retry budget.
chatPanel.fallback_auto_hint: Auto (default) lets the backend route to an available model. A fallback swap is announced in chat and sticks until your model recovers. Disabled turns fallback off.
chatPanel.refusal_fallback_desc: When your current model's content filter declines a message, retry it once on this model. Your primary model returns on the next message.
chatPanel.refusal_fallback_auto_hint: Auto retries on the model the provider suggests in its refusal, when it names one. The retry is announced in chat. Disabled shows the refusal as before.
chatPanel.failed_to_save_refusal_fallback_model: Failed to save content-filter fallback model
chatPanel.session_card_source_links: PR and Issue Chips on Session Cards
chatPanel.session_card_source_links_desc: Show a chip on each session's sidebar card for every pull request, merge request and issue mentioned in that session. Turning it off also stops the periodic provider calls that keep those chips up to date.
chatPanel.feature_videos_cached: Saved on this device: {{cached}} of {{total}} · release {{release}}
chatPanel.feature_videos_downloads_disabled: Video downloads are turned off. Only clips already saved will play.
chatPanel.failed_to_load_feature_video_status: Failed to load feature-video cache status
chatPanel.message_font_size_desc: Font size for the conversation, in every session: message text, code, tables, suggested replies and the message input. The Compact content width grows to match. Sidebar, session list and the rest of the interface are unaffected.
chatPanel.kiro_harness_fallback_body: When using a Kiro harness, the fallbacks you manage on app.kiro.dev run first, inside the harness. The fallbacks below are {{productName}}'s own and run only if the turn still fails after that.
chatPanel.follow_default_description: Older chats can keep the model they first ran on and ignore a new default. Chats that mates, apps, schedules or channels started keep their model. You see how many will change and confirm before anything changes.
chatPanel.follow_default_button: Make my chats follow the default
chatPanel.follow_default_none: All your chats already follow the Default Model setting.
chatPanel.follow_default_confirm_body: Each one stops using its own model, even one you picked yourself. Chats that mates, apps, schedules or channels started are not included. This can't be undone, but you can still pick a model in any chat.
chatPanel.follow_default_hint: Only chats you started yourself are counted.
chatPanel.follow_default_confirm_target: From their next message, they use the Default Model setting: <model/>.
chatPanel.follow_default_confirm_target_auto: From their next message, they use Auto: the model from the agent configuration, or the system default when none is configured.
chatPanel.follow_default_done_one: {{count}} chat now follows the Default Model setting.
chatPanel.follow_default_done_other: {{count}} chats now follow the Default Model setting.
chatPanel.follow_default_changed: Nothing was changed. Some chats changed after the count. Press the button again to see the new count.
chatPanel.follow_default_failed: Couldn't update the chats. Try again.

displayPanel.native_window_zoom_tip: Native window zoom, the same setting as {{mod}}+ / {{mod}}− (50%–300%). Remembered across launches.
displayPanel.custom_font_family_desc: The font the whole dashboard uses, including chat, the composer, and sidebar session and folder names. Pick one installed on the machine you view the dashboard from, or type any font name — a Nerd Font renders its glyphs and a programming font shows its ligatures.
displayPanel.custom_font_detect_added: Installed fonts added to the list.
displayPanel.custom_font_detect_none: No fonts beyond the ones already listed.
displayPanel.custom_font_detect_denied: Font access was not granted — the list keeps the fonts already detected, and you can still type any font name.
displayPanel.custom_font_ligatures_desc: Render programming ligatures (=>, !=, ->) when the custom font has them. Code and diffs in messages are unaffected.
displayPanel.translucent_panels_desc: Show the top bar, the tab bar, the message box, the suggestion chips and the search fields as frosted glass over the content that scrolls under them. Off, they are solid cards.
displayPanel.terminal_font_family_desc: Font for the built-in terminal. Pick one installed on the machine you view the dashboard from, or type any font name — a Nerd Font renders Powerline and prompt-theme glyphs.
displayPanel.terminal_font_detect_added: Installed fonts added to the list.
displayPanel.terminal_font_detect_none: No fonts beyond the ones already listed.
displayPanel.terminal_font_detect_denied: Font access was not granted — the list keeps the fonts already detected, and you can still type any font name.
displayPanel.terminal_font_size_desc: Text size in the built-in terminal, measured in pixels.
displayPanel.terminal_cursor_style_desc: Shape of the terminal cursor. Bar and underline leave the character under it visible.
displayPanel.terminal_shell_hint: The shell the built-in terminal launches.
displayPanel.terminal_shell_desc: An absolute path or a command on PATH. Leave empty to use the system default ($SHELL).
displayPanel.terminal_shell_not_executable: Not an executable shell — enter an absolute path or a command on PATH, or leave empty for the system default.
displayPanel.terminal_shell_save_failed: Could not save the shell setting
displayPanel.terminal_completion_desc: Show the completion popup while typing in the Terminal. Enter runs the line you typed; to take a suggestion, press ↑/↓ then Enter, or Tab. Off hides the popup; your shell's own Tab completion still works.
displayPanel.terminal_completion_save_failed: Could not save the command completion setting
displayPanel.terminal_reuse_current_desc: Copies the command instead of running it: Run in terminal focuses the terminal tab you have selected and copies the command, so you can paste it into that shell while keeping its working directory, environment, and any active login session. With no terminal open, it still copies the command for you to paste — it is never run for you.
displayPanel.terminal_reuse_current_save_failed: Could not save the terminal reuse setting
displayPanel.terminal_external_app_desc: Adds an option to the Files tab’s ⋯ menu that opens this app in the project’s folder. Lists only supported apps installed on this computer.
displayPanel.terminal_external_app_none_found: No supported terminal app was found on this computer.
displayPanel.terminal_external_app_save_failed: Could not save the external terminal app
displayPanel.terminal_external_app_detect_failed: Couldn't check which terminal apps are installed on this computer.
displayPanel.config_load_failed: Could not load the saved display settings. The shell, recent-session and command completion settings are unavailable until it loads.
displayPanel.installed_themes_load_failed: Could not load the theme list; retrying automatically. Until it loads, an installed theme cannot be selected or applied.
displayPanel.installed_themes_refresh_failed: Could not refresh the theme list. It is out of date.
displayPanel.installed_themes_refresh_failed_after_in: The theme was installed, but the theme list could not be refreshed. Press Retry to refresh the list and apply it, or pick it from the theme list once it refreshes.
displayPanel.show_unread_dot: Show unread dot on session cards
displayPanel.show_unread_dot_save_failed: Could not save the unread dot setting.
displayPanel.recent_tint_save_failed: Could not save the recent-session highlight count.

instancesPanel.connect_disabled_needs_restart: The gateway is on but not active yet — restart it to connect.
instancesPanel.connect_needs_restart: Connect to {{id}} failed: the gateway needs a restart first. See the note below.
instancesPanel.connected_switch_from_tab_strip: Connected “{{name}}”. Switch to it from the tab strip in the top header.
instancesPanel.connection_did_not_complete_try_diagnose: Connection did not complete. Try Diagnose for details.
instancesPanel.default_destination_hint: “Send a copy to” lists this crew first, marked as the default. A folder can choose its own.
instancesPanel.default_destination_save_failed: Couldn't save the default destination crew.

remoteCrewPanel.auto_connect_desc: When on, opening the web app connects every crew automatically, and reconnects them when you come back to the tab. Turn off to connect a crew only when you switch to it.
remoteCrewPanel.launch_status_unavailable: Could not refresh the setup progress. The card below shows the last state received.
remoteCrewPanel.copy_policy_failed: Could not copy the policy JSON to the clipboard. Try again, or allow clipboard access for this site.

privacyPanel.recordMetricsDescriptionExporting: Collect performance metrics and send them to the configured metrics collectors.
privacyPanel.recordMetricsSaveFailed: Could not change this setting. Try again.

privacyPanel.recordMetricsEgressOn: Metrics are being sent off this machine, to the collectors listed below.
