privacyPanel.recordMetricsEgressOff: Metrics collectors are configured, so recording would also send metrics off this machine. Turn it on in config.json if that is what you want.
privacyPanel.recordMetricsStatusUnavailable: Could not load the metric-recording setting. The switch is locked until it loads.

notificationsPanel.notify_when_a_background_chat_finishes: Notify when a background chat finishes
notificationsPanel.notify_when_a_background_chat_finishes_d: Shows a system notification naming the chat that finished, but only while this window is minimized or behind another app.
notificationsPanel.unread_only_when_done_or_waiting: Mark sessions unread only when they need you
notificationsPanel.unread_only_when_done_or_waiting_descrip: A background session is marked unread when its agent finishes or waits on your answer, instead of on every new message.
notificationsPanel.always_interrupts_cannot_be_muted_or_low: Always interrupts — cannot be muted or lowered
notificationsPanel.channel_not_active_app_disabled_setting_: Channel not active (app disabled) — setting retained
notificationsPanel.category_agent_description: When the agent proactively messages you outside a chat
notificationsPanel.category_all_description: Fallback sound when no category-specific override is set
notificationsPanel.category_approval_description: When the agent needs a tool approval or an answer
notificationsPanel.category_skills_description: New skill candidates awaiting your approval
notificationsPanel.category_turn_description: When a conversation finishes and hands control back to you. Agent questions use the “Approvals and questions” sound instead.
notificationsPanel.category_dictation_description: Plays a sound when dictation stops before you end it
notificationsPanel.failed_to_save_channel_setting: Failed to save the channel setting. The previous value was restored.
notificationsPanel.system_notifications_description: Show notifications on your desktop even when this window is in the background.
notificationsPanel.system_notifications_blocked: Blocked in your browser. Turn it back on in the site's permission settings.
notificationsPanel.show_banner_for_new_notifications: Show a banner for new notifications
notificationsPanel.show_banner_for_new_notifications_descri: A card slides in under the top bar when a notification arrives, then tucks into the bell.
notificationsPanel.custom_sounds_description: Make your own sound so you can tell your {{productName}} apart from others nearby. Each sound you save appears in every sound list under Per-category sounds.
notificationsPanel.custom_sound_none: No sounds yet. Add one below from an audio file or from tones.
notificationsPanel.custom_sound_tones_hint: Each tone is one note. Pitch is in Hz (higher sounds sharper). Start and Length are in seconds. Volume runs from 0 to 1.
notificationsPanel.custom_sound_error_name: Use 1 to {{max}} letters, digits, spaces, dashes or underscores.
notificationsPanel.custom_sound_error_freq: Each pitch must be {{min}} to {{max}} Hz.
notificationsPanel.custom_sound_error_dur: Each length must be {{min}} to {{max}} seconds.
notificationsPanel.custom_sound_error_gain: Each volume must be above 0 and at most 1.
notificationsPanel.custom_sound_error_start: Each tone must start at 0 or later and end within {{max}} seconds.
notificationsPanel.custom_sound_error_too_many: You can keep up to {{max}} custom sounds.
notificationsPanel.custom_sound_error_save: Could not save the sound. Free up space for this site in your browser settings, then try again.
notificationsPanel.custom_sound_error_delete: Could not delete the sound. Free up space for this site in your browser settings, then try again.
notificationsPanel.custom_sound_error_undo: Could not bring the sound back. Free up space for this site in your browser settings, then try again.
notificationsPanel.custom_sound_starter: Starting example. Change it to make your own sound.
notificationsPanel.sound_save_failed: Could not save the sound setting. Free up space for this site in your browser settings, then try again.
notificationsPanel.custom_sound_file_hint: MP3, WAV or OGG, up to {{maxKb}} KB and {{maxSeconds}} seconds. It stays in this browser and is never uploaded.
notificationsPanel.custom_sound_error_file_size: The file must be {{max}} KB or smaller.
notificationsPanel.custom_sound_error_file_length: The sound must be {{max}} seconds or shorter.
notificationsPanel.custom_sound_error_file_decode: This browser can't play that file. Try an MP3, WAV or OGG file.
notificationsPanel.custom_sound_error_file_gone: That sound's file is no longer stored in this browser, so it can't be brought back.
notificationsPanel.custom_sound_choose_where: Choose where it plays in Per-category sounds

securityPanel.disabling_weakens_protection: Disabling "{{name}}" weakens protection against destructive or credential-exfiltration commands. Some commands may stay blocked by independent defense-in-depth controls.
securityPanel.other_surfaces_have_their_own_profiles: A surface with its own profile can allow what the host cannot: {{surfaces}}.
securityPanel.profile_unusable_body: A profile named below could not be loaded, so its surface is held at the policy fallback ceiling — deny-all unless a looser fallback is declared. Correct the file in the profiles folder of your {{productName}} data home — it is reloaded automatically.
securityPanel.profile_unusable_detail: The file was unreadable, failed to parse, or extends a profile that is missing. A restart is only needed if the file is already valid for a newer build than the one running.
securityPanel.disabling_all_built_in_denies_removes_ki: Disabling all built-in denies removes {{productName}}’s protection against destructive and credential-exfiltration commands. Some commands may stay blocked by independent defense-in-depth controls (sensitive paths, IMDS, git-publish).
securityPanel.unknown_scopes_title: Profile scopes not in this build
securityPanel.unknown_scopes_tip: These profiles name capability scopes this build does not register — typically scopes a companion edition adds, though a misspelled scope key lands here too. They are skipped and have no effect in this build.
securityPanel.distribution_tip: Your administrator publishes one policy centrally. This host fetches it, keeps the last copy so an outage cannot remove the ceiling, and re-fetches on a schedule. The address is not shown.
securityPanel.distribution_polling_stopped: Background refresh is not running — changes apply at next restart
securityPanel.distribution_refresh_applied: Last refresh installed a new ceiling
securityPanel.distribution_refresh_rejected: Last refresh was refused — run `kirocrew policy fetch` for the reason
securityPanel.distribution_refresh_unreachable: Source was unreachable on the last refresh
securityPanel.distribution_refresh_not_configured: No central source to refresh from
securityPanel.distribution_error_misconfigured: Distribution settings could not be read
securityPanel.distribution_awaiting_policy: Set up to fetch a central policy, but none is in effect yet. No enterprise ceiling restricts the host surface until one applies.
securityPanel.rules_read_the_command_line_not_the_prog: These rules only read the command line itself. A command tucked inside a program that the line runs is never read, so it is not matched. A pattern here adds friction to a direct command line; the OS-level sandbox is the layer that fences the action off.
securityPanel.turn_off_every_rule: Turn off every built-in denied-command rule at once. Independent defense-in-depth controls (sensitive paths, IMDS, git-publish) stay enforced.
securityPanel.turn_off_every_rule_governance_locked: Turn off every built-in denied-command rule at once. Independent defense-in-depth controls (sensitive paths, IMDS, git-publish) stay enforced, and rules pinned by your organization’s policy remain on.
securityPanel.feature_credential_redaction_description: Scans every output path for plaintext and base64-encoded AWS keys, private keys, and provider tokens
securityPanel.feature_csrf_description: Origin/Referer validation on all POST/PUT/DELETE requests and WebSocket connections
securityPanel.feature_denied_commands_description: Built-in regex patterns blocking destructive and credential-exfiltrating CLI operations (configurable below)
securityPanel.feature_enterprise_grid_description: Two-layer defense against data exfiltration to personal/external Slack workspaces
securityPanel.feature_mcp_validation_description: Type-safe schemas, unicode normalization, length limits, and unknown field rejection on every tool handler
securityPanel.feature_observe_mode_description: Only owner/allowlisted messages recorded in shared channels — prevents context poisoning
securityPanel.feature_os_sandbox_description: User + mount namespace isolation (Linux) / Seatbelt sandbox (macOS) hides credential paths from agent subprocesses
securityPanel.feature_sel_audit_description: Immutable, HMAC-chained security event trail with credential redaction before forwarding
securityPanel.feature_sensitive_paths_description: Credential directories and {{productName}} trust roots blocked at the hook layer before tool execution
securityPanel.feature_suspicious_patterns_description: Detects deletion, exfiltration, and pipe-execution attack shapes in shell commands
securityPanel.feature_token_auth_description: HMAC-SHA256 signed, IP-pinned, single-use tokens with dual expiry on the link and the session
securityPanel.feature_url_exfil_description: Domain-agnostic scanning for suspicious query strings, base64 blobs, and credential patterns in URLs
securityPanel.enforced_by_floor: Enforced by an always-on protection built into {{productName}}
securityPanel.pinned_by_policy: Enforced by your organization's security policy
securityPanel.edition_rule_tooltip: Added by this installation's edition, not the built-in catalog. On by default, and you can switch it off.
securityPanel.pinned_for_the_host_surface: Set by the host-surface profile. This is the ceiling for in-process host actions only — other surfaces have their own profiles and may allow this.
securityPanel.yolo_duration_desc: Applies whenever you turn auto-approve on from the dashboard, Slack, or the API — all of them use this one duration.
securityPanel.yolo_duration_next_activation_note: Applies the next time you turn auto-approve on.
securityPanel.yolo_active_until_restart: Auto-approve is on and stays on until {{productName}} restarts.
securityPanel.third_party_apps_unavailable: Could not read the current setting, so it cannot be shown or changed here. If it was already on, third-party apps stay allowed — reload the page to try again.
securityPanel.third_party_apps_on_warning: This trusts every third-party app, including ones you install later — not just the one you were trying to start. A trusted app runs with the same access {{productName}} has: your files, your saved credentials, and the internet.
securityPanel.third_party_apps_scope_note: Takes effect immediately. Switching it back off also stops the apps it was admitting — their shutdown hooks run, their backends are stopped, and anything that could not be stopped is reported back to you.
securityPanel.custom_patterns_hidden_by_filter: Your custom patterns are hidden by the current filter.
securityPanel.built_in_rules_enforced_note: {{enabled}} of {{total}} built-in rules are currently enforced, after your opt-outs and any policy pins.
securityPanel.custom_patterns_counted_separately: Your custom patterns are counted separately in Denied Commands.
securityPanel.tailnet_desc: Adds this machine's Tailscale MagicDNS name to the dashboard's allowed origins, so a request arriving through tailscale serve passes the CSRF origin check instead of being refused.
securityPanel.tailnet_pin_caveat: The per-device session pin cannot bind behind tailscale serve: every request reaches {{productName}} from 127.0.0.1, so a dashboard link works from any device on your tailnet, not only the one it was opened on. Treat the link as a password.
securityPanel.tailnet_restart_note: The name is resolved once, when {{productName}} starts, so a change here takes effect on the next restart.
securityPanel.tailnet_tip: This only affects the origin allow-list. It does not start Tailscale, open a port, or share the dashboard with anyone; you still run tailscale serve yourself.
securityPanel.tailnet_unavailable: Could not read the tailnet setting, so it cannot be shown or changed here. If it was already on, the tailnet name stays allowed; reload the page to try again.
securityPanel.tailnet_unresolved_note: This is on, but no tailnet name was resolved when {{productName}} started, so nothing was added to the allowed origins. A dashboard reached through tailscale serve is still refused by the origin check. Restart {{productName}} once the name is available.

trustedApps.description: Apps you have allowed to run their own code on this computer. Trust covers one app at a time; every other third-party app stays blocked.
trustedApps.revoke_hint: Removing trust also switches the app off.
trustedApps.allow_all_description: Off by default. When on, every third-party app you install can run its own code straight away, without asking you first.
trustedApps.revoke_disables: {{name}} is no longer trusted and has been switched off.
trustedApps.change_failed: That change did not take effect: {{detail}}
trustedApps.revoke_confirm_body: “{{name}}” will be switched off and stop working. It stays installed, and you can trust it again later.
trustedApps.allow_all_confirm_body: Allowing every third-party app lets any app you install run its own code inside {{productName}}, with the same access {{productName}} has — your files, your saved credentials, and the internet. Trusting one app at a time is safer.
trustedApps.allow_all_confirm_ack: I understand every third-party app I install will be able to run its own code with {{productName}}'s access.
trustedApps.ineffective_description: These names were saved as trusted, but {{productName}} does not accept them, so the apps are still blocked. Remove them to tidy the list.

trustedRegistries.change_failed: That change did not take effect: {{detail}}
trustedRegistries.corrupt_notice: The trust file is damaged, so no registry is trusted. Open {{path}} to see which registries you trusted, then delete it and trust them again.
trustedRegistries.description: An app registry you added by hand reads its list of apps without your Git credentials, so an app kept in a private repository shows no pictures and cannot be installed. Trusting a registry lets {{productName}} use your own Git credentials for the repositories that registry lists.
trustedRegistries.empty: No registries added by hand. Add one under <store>Apps</store>.
trustedRegistries.grant_confirm_body: “{{name}}” will use your own Git credentials when it downloads the repositories it lists. The trust covers every branch of this registry's repository, not just the one shown. The people who write that registry choose which repositories those are, so they choose which of your private repositories get downloaded. You can remove this trust again at any time.
trustedRegistries.grant_confirm_ok: Trust it with my Git credentials
trustedRegistries.not_served: Not listed — this registry is not shown in the App Store, so it cannot be trusted.
trustedRegistries.not_served_not_configured: Not configured — this registry is not in your config any more, but it is still trusted. Remove trust to clear it.
trustedRegistries.not_served_pinned_name: Not used — a registry that comes with {{productName}} already has this name. Rename this one under <apps>Apps</apps> to use it.
trustedRegistries.pinned_note: Registries that come with {{productName}} are not shown here, because the build already trusts those.
trustedRegistries.section_title: Registries trusted with your Git credentials
trustedRegistries.unavailable: Could not read which registries are trusted.
trustedRegistries.unknown_registry: This registry was removed from Apps, so it can't be trusted.

securityPanel.yolo_duration_load_failed: Could not load the saved duration. The highlighted option is the default, not what is stored.
securityPanel.tailnet_copy_failed: Copy failed. Select the address and copy it manually.
securityPanel.distribution_error_misconfigured_detail: The central policy declaration on this host could not be parsed, so no ceiling is being fetched.
securityPanel.distribution_refresh_rejected_detail: The last policy refresh was rejected by the source.
securityPanel.distribution_refresh_unreachable_detail: The last policy refresh could not reach the source.
securityPanel.denied_commands_load_failed: Could not load the denied-command rules. The lists below are empty because the read failed, not because there are no rules.
securityPanel.credential_redaction_toggle: Redact credentials in files the dashboard opens for you
securityPanel.credential_redaction_toggle_help: Off shows files the dashboard opens for you — the chat side panel's Files tab, and the Library and Artifacts previews — as written, in your own dashboard only. On by default. Conversations in this dashboard, Slack, and messaging channels stay redacted. Changing it reloads the files you have open (unsaved edits are kept) and closes file-comparison (diff) views.
securityPanel.credential_redaction_off_notice: Files you open are shown unredacted; chat and messaging channels stay redacted.
securityPanel.credential_redaction_read_failed: Could not read the redaction setting. Nothing is shown here because the read failed, not because redaction is off. The 'Open a chat with the agent' link shares only this error message.
securityPanel.credential_redaction_write_failed: Could not save the change. {{state}} The 'Open a chat with the agent' link shares only this error message.
securityPanel.credential_redaction_desc_intro: {{productName}} redacts anything that looks like a credential — access keys, tokens, private keys — from agent output before you see it. When it redacts a value of your own that you need to read back, these four steps get it in front of you.
securityPanel.credential_redaction_step_write: Ask the agent to write the value to a file.
securityPanel.credential_redaction_step_open: Open that file from the Files tab of the chat side panel.
securityPanel.credential_redaction_desc_tail: This is separate from the Secrets page, which stores values for the agent to use. This setting only controls whether you see credential-shaped values in the files the dashboard opens for you. Links that look like they carry data out — for example an approval link with a long token in its URL — stay redacted either way, and every command-blocking rule stays enforced.
securityPanel.credential_redaction_owner_only: Only the dashboard owner can read or change this setting. The 'Open a chat with the agent' link shares only this error message.
securityPanel.credential_redaction_ask_agent: Open a chat with the agent about this error

skillsPanel.config_load_failed: Could not load the skills settings. The switches show defaults, not what is stored.

sttSettings.transcribe_vocabulary_hint: Names and terms you uploaded to Amazon Transcribe so dictation spells them right. Listed from the AWS profile and region above.
sttSettings.transcribe_vocabulary_language_mismatch: This vocabulary is for {{vocabularyLanguage}}, but dictation is set to {{dictationLanguage}}. Amazon Transcribe refuses a vocabulary in another language, so dictation will fail until you choose another one or None.
sttSettings.transcribe_vocabulary_language_mismatch_: This vocabulary is for {{vocabularyLanguage}}, which is not one of your Mixed languages ({{languages}}). Amazon Transcribe refuses a vocabulary in another language, so streaming dictation will fail until you choose another one or None.
sttSettings.transcribe_vocabulary_unavailable: Amazon Transcribe has no ready vocabulary named {{name}} in {{region}}. Dictation will fail until you choose another one or None.
sttSettings.transcribe_vocabulary_access_denied: These AWS credentials are not allowed to list custom vocabularies. Grant {{permission}} to see them here.
sttSettings.transcribe_vocabulary_list_failed: Your custom vocabularies could not be loaded from AWS.
sttSettings.transcribe_languages_hint: Languages people switch between in one recording, such as Vietnamese and English. With two or more picked, dictation detects the language of each part and transcribes it in that language. Streaming dictation only, one dialect per language.
sttSettings.transcribe_languages_one: {{name}}: pick one more to turn on
sttSettings.transcribe_languages_pending: Pick a second language to detect both. Until then, dictation uses the language above.
sttSettings.transcribe_languages_limit: Limit of {{max}} reached. Deselect one to pick another.
sttSettings.language_overridden_by_mixed: While Mixed languages is on, this language is used only for voice messages and for dictation when Streaming is off.
sttSettings.endpointing_desc: Use a fast model to detect when you've finished a complete request and send it automatically. Streaming providers only.
sttSettings.submit_on_release_desc: Stopping sends the message. Shift-click the mic, or slide sideways on the phone, to keep a draft.
sttSettings.provider_desc: Local speech recognition runs on this machine and sends nothing anywhere. Transcribe streams your audio to AWS.
sttSettings.retention_on_device: No. It is processed on this machine and not saved.
sttSettings.retention_on_device_detail: The text you dictate is saved with your message, like anything you type. A recording that fails to transcribe stays only in this browser tab, so you can retry or save it, until you close the tab.
sttSettings.retention_transcribe: Not by {{productName}} or in your AWS account. AWS may keep a copy to improve its services.
sttSettings.retention_transcribe_detail: Audio is streamed to Amazon Transcribe, so no transcription job or file is created in your account, which is why the Transcribe console shows nothing. Opting out needs an AI services opt-out policy in AWS Organizations; it stops AWS keeping voice inputs and deletes what it kept for that purpose.
sttSettings.streaming_desc: Show the transcript in the input box as you speak, instead of only when you stop.
sttSettings.model_download_prompt: Not on this machine yet: a one-time {{size}} download. Fetching it now avoids a wait during your first dictation.
sttSettings.custom_model_path_desc: Set up your own speech model file in three steps.
sttSettings.custom_model_path_desc_no_dir: Your own speech model file, placed in the speech models folder.
sttSettings.custom_model_path_step_get: Get a speech model file (.bin) from whisper.cpp on Hugging Face.
sttSettings.custom_model_path_step_get_sha: Each file's page there lists its SHA-256.
sttSettings.custom_model_path_step_place: Put it in the speech models folder below.
sttSettings.custom_model_path_step_name: Type its file name in the box above (for example ggml-medium.en-q5_0.bin).
sttSettings.custom_model_path_hint: A wrong name is refused and nothing else changes. Only whisper.cpp .bin model files work.
sttSettings.custom_model_sha256_desc: Paste the SHA-256 shown on the file's download page. It checks the file is the one you downloaded.
sttSettings.custom_model_sha256_how: Copy it from the download page, where it is usually listed next to the file. Or open a terminal in the folder from step 2, run the command for your system below, and paste what it prints.
sttSettings.custom_model_sha256_hint: A wrong value is refused and nothing else changes.
sttSettings.custom_model_incomplete: Add both the file name and the SHA-256 to use your custom model. Until then, {{model}} stays in use.
sttSettings.custom_model_refused: Not saved: {{reason}} Voice input keeps using {{model}}.
sttSettings.custom_model_not_used: Not used while {{model}} is selected. Pick Custom to use this file.
sttSettings.download_failed: The download could not be started.
sttSettings.unavailable_disabled: Speech-to-text is turned off. Switch it on above.
sttSettings.unavailable_provider_off: Voice is on, but the provider is set to Off, so nothing is listening. Pick another provider from the Provider menu below.
sttSettings.unavailable_extra_missing: The voice packages are not installed in the gateway's Python environment.
sttSettings.unavailable_no_wheel: There is no prebuilt speech recogniser for this platform. Install a C++ compiler and CMake, then reinstall the voice packages.
sttSettings.unavailable_import_failed: The speech recogniser is installed but could not be loaded on this machine.
sttSettings.unavailable_unsupported_cpu: The speech recogniser can't run on this computer's processor, so it is not loaded. Pick "Transcribe (AWS)" in the Provider menu below (your audio goes to AWS and is billed to your AWS account), or switch off "Enabled" above. Installed {{productName}} with pip rather than the desktop app? You can instead rebuild the recogniser from source on this machine.
sttSettings.unavailable_load_crashed: The last attempt to load the speech model crashed {{productName}}, so it is not loaded again until the voice packages are reinstalled. Reinstall the voice packages, or pick another provider or Off from the Provider menu below.
sttSettings.unavailable_native_probe_crashed: The speech recogniser crashed while being checked, so it is not loaded. Reinstall the voice packages, or pick another provider or Off from the Provider menu below.
sttSettings.unavailable_model_missing: The speech model is not on this machine yet. Download it below.
sttSettings.unavailable_apple_unsupported: Apple Speech needs macOS 26 or newer. Choose the local provider instead.
sttSettings.unavailable_apple_needs_toolchain: Apple Speech needs the Xcode command line tools. Install them, then reload this page.
sttSettings.decoder_fetch_prompt: {{productName}} can fetch a digest-verified copy for this machine, so nothing has to be installed by hand.
sttSettings.config_load_failed: Could not load the speech-to-text settings.
sttSettings.status_unavailable: Could not check the speech-to-text status. The badge above shows the saved setting, not a live probe.
sttSettings.polish_desc: Sends the finished text, never the audio, to the AI model you already chat with, which fixes punctuation and capitalisation. Your words are never changed.
sttSettings.model_slow_on_cpu: Slower than real time on this machine, so the transcript lags behind your speech. Still the most accurate for multilingual and mixed-language input.
sttSettings.backend_encoder_only: {{name}} — partly accelerated, text step on CPU
sttSettings.backend_cpu_only: Runs on CPU — no GPU in this build
sttSettings.last_recognition_value: {{duration}} for the finished text, {{rtf}}× the audio length
sttSettings.decode_threads_desc: CPU threads the local model uses to recognise speech. Auto uses half of this machine's cores, at most 16. On a large machine with cores to spare, more threads finish each dictation sooner. A change applies at the next dictation, which reloads the model once.
sttSettings.decode_threads_env_override: This gateway uses {{value}} threads, set by KIROCREW_STT_THREADS. Remove that variable to use this choice.

teamsPanel.jwt_required: Microsoft Teams needs the PyJWT dependency. Inbound Bot Framework requests carry a signed token that has to be validated, so the channel refuses to start without it. If you have just installed it, restart the gateway to load it.
teamsPanel.save_failed_is_the_gateway_running: Save failed. Is the gateway running?
teamsPanel.saved_restart_the_gateway_to_apply: Saved. Restart the gateway to apply.
teamsPanel.settings_are_saved_but_the_channel_is_no: Settings are saved but the channel is not running. Restart the gateway to connect.
teamsPanel.teams_credential_check_failed: Teams credential check failed ({{error}}). Verify the App ID / password / tenant, then restart the gateway.
teamsPanel.where_to_find_the_client_secret: Where to find the client secret

voicePanel.could_not_read_the_hosts_voice_list_only: Could not read the host's voice list. Only the operating system default is offered.
voicePanel.the_built_in_engine_needs_no_setup_amazo: The built-in engine needs no setup; Amazon Polly uses AWS credentials + network
voicePanel.this_host_has_no_built_in_speech_engine_: This host has no built-in speech engine. Install espeak-ng (for example: sudo apt install espeak-ng), or pick another provider.
voicePanel.voice_catalogue_unavailable: Could not load the Polly voice list. The picker shows a built-in fallback list.
voicePanel.voice_from_the_hosts_built_in_speech_eng: Voice from the host's built-in speech engine
voicePanel.speech_rate_for_spoken_replies_built_in: Speech rate for spoken replies (built-in engine)
voicePanel.speech_rate_for_spoken_replies_polly: Speech rate for spoken replies (Amazon Polly)

iMessagePanel.allowed_handles_desc: Phone numbers or Apple Account emails allowed to message the agent. Empty denies everyone — anyone who knows this Mac's handle can send to it, so there is no safe default. Formatting is ignored.
iMessagePanel.cannot_load: Cannot load iMessage config. Is the gateway running?
iMessagePanel.connection_failed: iMessage did not start ({{error}}). Check that imsg is installed and that this process has Full Disk Access, then restart the gateway.
iMessagePanel.db_path_desc: Override where the Messages database is read from. Leave empty to use the default location.
iMessagePanel.empty_allowlist_hint: The channel is on but no handle is allowed, so it will reject every message. Add your own number or Apple Account email.
iMessagePanel.enable_desc: Start the channel at gateway boot on this Mac.
iMessagePanel.macos_only: iMessage needs macOS with Messages signed in, and the gateway must run on that Mac. This host cannot reach iMessage, so these settings are read-only.
iMessagePanel.managed_locally: iMessage settings are managed on the machine running {{productName}}, so they are read-only from a remote session.
iMessagePanel.prerequisites_body: No bot and no token: the agent reaches your own Messages app through a local bridge, so the transport involves no third party. Your prompts still go to the model provider the agent is configured with, as on any channel. You need macOS 14 or newer signed in to Messages, the imsg CLI installed, and two one-time macOS permissions — Full Disk Access and Automation for Messages.
iMessagePanel.save_failed: Save failed. Is the gateway running?
iMessagePanel.saved_but_not_running: Settings are saved but the channel is not running. Restart the gateway to connect.
iMessagePanel.saved_restart: Saved. Restart the gateway to apply.
iMessagePanel.service_desc: Which service outbound replies use. Inbound is unaffected — messages are accepted whichever service they arrive over.
iMessagePanel.tagline: Message your agents from the Messages app on any of your Apple devices. No bot, no token — the gateway drives Messages on this Mac.

webexPanel.connection_failed: Webex connection failed ({{error}}). Check the bot token and network access to webexapis.com, then restart the gateway.
webexPanel.save_failed_is_the_gateway_running: Save failed. Is the gateway running?
webexPanel.saved_restart_the_gateway_to_apply: Saved. Restart the gateway to apply.
webexPanel.settings_are_saved_but_the_channel_is_no: Settings are saved but the channel is not running. Restart the gateway to connect.
webexPanel.verified_with_webex_and_saved_restart_th: Verified with Webex and saved. Restart the gateway to connect.
webexPanel.where_to_find_the_bot_token: Where to find the bot token
webexPanel.empty_allowlist_hint: No allowed emails: the bot rejects every message. Add your Webex account email below.
webexPanel.soft_threshold_must_be_1_to_100: Soft context threshold must be a whole number between 1 and 100.
webexPanel.hard_threshold_must_be_1_to_100: Hard context threshold must be a whole number between 1 and 100.
webexPanel.soft_threshold_must_not_exceed_hard: Soft context threshold must not be higher than the hard one — the hard threshold is checked first, so a higher soft value would never be reached.
webexPanel.allow_group_spaces_desc: Off by default. A reply in a space is visible to everyone in it, including people not on the allowed-emails list.
webexPanel.allowed_room_ids_desc:
Empty means no space is answered, so turning the switch on alone grants nothing. The sender must also be on the allowed-emails list. A space ID is an opaque string — list yours with:
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $WEBEX_BOT_TOKEN" https://webexapis.com/v1/rooms
webexPanel.allowed_room_ids_empty_hint: No space is answered yet. Add the bot to the space, then paste that space's ID here.
webexPanel.reply_in_thread_desc: Reply under the message's own thread when it has one, which keeps a busy space readable.
webexPanel.soft_context_threshold_desc: When a conversation's context passes this, suggest /compact or /new instead of compacting automatically.
webexPanel.hard_context_threshold_desc: Compact automatically at this point, even without a decision, so the context window never overflows.

weixinPanel.could_not_reach_the_wechat_login_service: Could not reach the WeChat login service.
weixinPanel.could_not_start_the_login_flow: Could not start the login flow.
weixinPanel.created_for_you_when_you_turn_this_on_if: Created for you when you turn this on, if it does not exist yet.
weixinPanel.scan_status_poll_failing: Could not check whether the code was scanned. Still trying.

whatsAppPanel.scan_the_code_from_linked_devices: Scan the code with WhatsApp on your phone: Settings, Linked devices, Link a device.
whatsAppPanel.signed_in_restart_the_gateway_to_start_r: Paired. Restart the gateway to start receiving messages.
whatsAppPanel.talk_to_your_agent_from_your_own_whatsap: Talk to your agent from your own WhatsApp account, paired as a linked device. Messages the agent sends come from your number.
whatsAppPanel.could_not_start_the_login_flow: Could not start the pairing flow.
whatsAppPanel.allowed_numbers_empty_adds_nobody: Phone numbers (digits with country code, no plus sign) that may also chat with the agent. Empty adds nobody beyond you.
whatsAppPanel.created_for_you_when_you_turn_this_on_if: Created for you when you turn this on, if it does not already exist.
whatsAppPanel.group_participation_is_opt_in_per_group: Group participation is opt-in per group: mention mode replies only when tagged; rules mode can also help unprompted, with a cooldown. Uses the unofficial WhatsApp Web protocol; keep usage personal-scale.
whatsAppPanel.the_channel_is_enabled_but_not_running: The channel is enabled but not running. Restart the gateway.
whatsAppPanel.already_paired_unlink_then_restart: Already paired. To pair a different device, unlink this one below, then restart the gateway.
whatsAppPanel.the_link_was_revoked_restart_to_pair_aga: The link was revoked. Restart the gateway to pair a device again.
whatsAppPanel.blocked_number_cannot_pair: WhatsApp has blocked this number, so pairing cannot start.
whatsAppPanel.pairing_starts_when_the_channel_starts: A pairing code exists only while the channel is pairing, and pairing begins when the channel starts. Enable the channel below, then restart the gateway.
whatsAppPanel.the_channel_is_not_running_enable_and_re: The WhatsApp channel is not running. Enable it below, then restart the gateway.
whatsAppPanel.revokes_the_linked_device_on_your_accoun: Revokes this linked device on your WhatsApp account and deletes the local session. The agent stops reading and sending until a device is paired again.
whatsAppPanel.unlinked_restart_to_pair_again: Unlinked. Restart the gateway to pair a device again.
whatsAppPanel.unlinked_but_the_session_file_was_kept: Unlinked from WhatsApp, but the local session file could not be removed. Delete it under the data home before pairing again.
whatsAppPanel.whatsapp_refused_the_unlink_still_linked: WhatsApp refused the unlink, so the device is still linked and the local session was kept. Try again, or revoke the device from your phone under Linked devices.
whatsAppPanel.channel_not_running_so_nothing_was_unlin: The channel is not running, so nothing was unlinked. A linked device stays linked: revoke it from your phone under Linked devices.
whatsAppPanel.the_agent_ignores_every_group_not_listed: The agent ignores every group that is not listed here.
whatsAppPanel.your_groups_load_once_the_channel_is_con: Your groups appear here once the channel is connected.
whatsAppPanel.every_group_you_joined_is_already_listed: Every group you have joined is already listed.
whatsAppPanel.the_agent_stays_silent_unless_these_appl: Free text. The agent stays silent unless these rules clearly apply.
whatsAppPanel.unofficial_protocol_ban_risk: Unofficial protocol: WhatsApp may ban the linked number. Don't link a number you can't afford to lose.
whatsAppPanel.scan_status_poll_failing: Could not check whether the code was scanned. Still trying.
whatsAppPanel.groups_unavailable: Could not load the groups this account has joined.

channels.hard_below_soft_error: Hard context threshold must be at or above the soft context threshold
channels.hard_threshold_description: Compact automatically at this percentage, even without a reply, so the context window never overflows.
channels.hard_threshold_range_error: Hard context threshold must be a number between 1 and 100
channels.threshold_description: Prompt to {{compact}} or {{new}} when the session context passes this percentage.

discordPanel.allowlist_description: Discord user IDs permitted to run the agent in DMs, approved threads, or allowed channels. Empty = deny all (fail closed).
discordPanel.auto_thread_description: A message in an allowed channel opens a fresh public thread, and the turn runs there instead of in the shared channel.
discordPanel.auto_thread_off_hint: Auto-thread is off, so messages in the channels above are ignored. {{productName}} never answers in a shared channel itself.
discordPanel.channel_allowlist_description: Optional. Approved users may also run the agent from these shared server channels. Empty = no shared channels.
discordPanel.channel_help: With Developer Mode on, right-click the channel → <mono>Copy Channel ID</mono>. Use the channel's own ID, not the ID of a thread inside it.
discordPanel.channel_warning: A shared channel is a wider disclosure boundary than a thread: everyone who can see the channel, and everyone who can open the public thread a turn runs in, can read what the agent writes and what its tools print. Only add a channel whose entire membership may see that.
discordPanel.description: Talk to your agent from Discord DMs, approved server threads, or allowed server channels over the Gateway WebSocket. Every other server channel is ignored.
discordPanel.empty_allowlist_hint: No allowed user IDs: the bot rejects every message (fail closed). Add your Discord user ID below.
discordPanel.guide_body: Create an app in the Discord Developer Portal, then copy the token from the <mono>Bot</mono> page. For DMs only, leave privileged intents off. For server threads, enable <mono>Message Content Intent</mono> and install with the <mono>bot</mono> and <mono>applications.commands</mono> scopes plus View Channel, Read Message History, and Send Messages in Threads. Enable Discord Developer Mode, then right-click your name to copy your numeric user ID.
discordPanel.reactions_description: Mark your message with an emoji for the phase the agent is in (queued → thinking → coding → done). Off leaves your message unmarked.
discordPanel.thinking_description: Post a preview of the model's reasoning as its own subtext note above the answer. Off keeps the channel to the answer alone.
discordPanel.thread_allowlist_description: Optional. Approved users may run the agent only in these exact Discord threads. Empty = DMs only.
discordPanel.thread_help: With Developer Mode on, right-click the thread → <mono>Copy Channel ID</mono>. Use the thread's ID, not its parent channel ID.
discordPanel.thread_warning: Thread mode enables Discord's global Message Content intent. Discord delivers content from every server channel the bot can see; {{productName}} discards traffic outside approved threads. Everyone who can view an approved thread can read agent replies and tool output.
discordPanel.threshold_description: Prompt to !compact or !new when the session context passes this percentage.
discordPanel.token_description: From the Developer Portal's Bot page (Reset Token to view it once).

telegramPanel.allowlist_description: Numeric Telegram user IDs permitted to DM the bot. Empty = deny all (fail closed): a Telegram bot is globally reachable by @username.
telegramPanel.description: Talk to your agent from Telegram over the Bot API (long-polling — no webhook or public address needed). Add allowed user IDs so the bot can respond.
telegramPanel.empty_allowlist_hint: No allowed user IDs: the bot rejects every message (fail closed). Add your numeric Telegram user ID below.
telegramPanel.forum_activation_description: When the bot replies inside an allow-listed topic. A direct message is always answered, whichever option is selected here.
telegramPanel.forum_activation_hint: Choose Only when addressed to hold a conversation with other people in the same topic — the bot then answers only when its @handle is used, or when one of its own messages is replied to.
telegramPanel.forum_allowlist_description: Numeric supergroup chat_ids permitted to run forum-topic sessions. These are negative (e.g. -1001234567890) — find one by adding a bot like @getidsbot to the group. Empty = deny all groups (fail closed).
telegramPanel.forum_empty_hint: Forum enabled but no allow-listed chats: all forum traffic is denied. Add your supergroup chat_id (a negative number like -100…).
telegramPanel.forum_toggle_description: Route each Topic of an allow-listed supergroup to its own agent session (Slack-thread style). Create a supergroup, turn on `Topics`, add the bot, then list the supergroup's `chat_id` below. The General topic and ordinary (non-forum) groups are always denied.
telegramPanel.forum_toggle_label: Serve forum Topics as per-Topic sessions
telegramPanel.guide_body: Message `@BotFather` on Telegram, send `/newbot`, and follow the prompts. BotFather replies with a bot token — paste it below. To find your numeric user ID, message `@userinfobot`.
telegramPanel.show_thinking_description: After each answer, post the reasoning as a collapsed quote you can expand. Off by default: Telegram's rate limit is per chat and shared with the streaming edits the answer already spends, so this costs one extra message per turn.
telegramPanel.token_description: From @BotFather after creating your bot (looks like 110201543:AAHdqT…).
telegramPanel.voice_replies_description: Send each answer as a voice message as well as text, using your voice_reply provider settings. Off by default: it costs a second message per turn against Telegram's per-chat rate budget, and text-to-speech may not be installed. Short answers are never spoken, and the text reply always lands first. Use /voice on or /voice off to change one conversation.

weComPanel.allow_all_bypass_note: Allow-all is on: the userid list above is bypassed. It is kept for when you switch back.
weComPanel.allow_all_description: Let everyone in your WeCom organization DM the bot without listing each userid. A WeCom AI bot is only reachable inside your own org tenant, but this grants agent access to the whole company — leave off for a per-person allow-list.
weComPanel.allowlist_description: WeCom userids (账号) permitted to DM the bot. Empty = deny all (fail closed).
weComPanel.bot_id_description: The Bot ID from your AI bot’s settings page in the WeCom admin console.
weComPanel.description: Talk to your agent from WeCom through a WeCom (企业微信) AI bot. The connection is an outbound WebSocket — no callback URL or open port to manage.
weComPanel.empty_allowlist_hint: No allowed userids: the bot rejects every message (fail closed). Add your WeCom userid below.
weComPanel.guide_body: In the WeCom admin console, open <mono>应用管理 → AI 智能体</mono> and create a bot. Its settings page shows a <mono>Bot ID</mono> and a <mono>Secret</mono> — paste both below. Every WeCom member has a <mono>userid</mono> (账号) for the allow-list.
weComPanel.token_description: The Secret shown next to the Bot ID on the same settings page.

feishuPanel.allowlist_description: Feishu open_ids permitted to DM the bot. Empty = deny all (fail closed).
feishuPanel.allow_group_description: Serve group conversations as well as direct messages. The bot only sees a group message when it is <mono>@</mono>-mentioned, and only in the groups listed below.
feishuPanel.app_id_description: The App ID from your custom app’s Credentials page in the Feishu developer console.
feishuPanel.app_secret_description: The App Secret shown next to the App ID on the same Credentials page.
feishuPanel.description: Talk to your agent from Feishu (飞书) or Lark through a custom app. The connection is an outbound WebSocket — no callback URL or open port to manage.
feishuPanel.empty_allowlist_hint: No allowed open_ids: the bot rejects every message (fail closed). Add your Feishu open_id below.
feishuPanel.group_allowlist_description: Feishu group chat_ids allowed to drive a turn. Empty = no group is served.
feishuPanel.group_empty_hint: Group chats are on but no chat_id is listed, so no group is served. Add a chat_id, or turn the toggle off.
feishuPanel.guide_body: In the Feishu developer console, create a <mono>custom app</mono> and open its <mono>Credentials & Basic Info</mono> page for the <mono>App ID</mono> and <mono>App Secret</mono> — paste both below. Then enable the <mono>Long connection</mono> event mode and subscribe to <mono>im.message.receive_v1</mono>. Each member’s <mono>open_id</mono> goes in the allow-list. The channel also needs its optional dependency: run <mono>pip install "lark-oapi>=1.4,<2"</mono> in the environment that runs the gateway, then restart it.

shortcutsPanel.custom_hint: Use at least one modifier key.
shortcutsPanel.turn_keyboard_shortcuts_on_or_off_global: Turn keyboard shortcuts on or off globally — {{chord}} (this reference) always works
shortcutsPanel.skips_shell_hint: Works inside the terminal too, so your shell stops receiving this key — do not pick Ctrl+C or Ctrl+R.
shortcutsPanel.skips_shell_hint_mac: Works inside the terminal too, so your shell stops receiving this key — do not pick ⌃C (Ctrl+C) or ⌃R (Ctrl+R).

browserPanel.node_missing: Needs Node.js 20 or newer, and no Node was found on this machine.
browserPanel.node_how: Install it, then reopen this page. <dl>Download Node.js</dl>
browserPanel.node_no_admin: On a machine where you cannot install Node — no admin rights, or a registry that needs a login — run the command below on the machine where {{productName}} is running. The script installs Node and the CLI into your home directory, and tells you how to fix it if your network blocks the download.
browserPanel.builtin_save_failed: Could not save the built-in browser setting.
browserPanel.builtin_status_unavailable: Could not load the built-in browser setting.
browserPanel.host_unavailable: Could not load the host name.
browserPanel.copy_failed: Copy failed. Select the command and copy it manually.
browserPanel.engine_download_failed: Could not start the browser download.
browserPanel.token_save_failed: Could not save the extension token.
browserPanel.managed_explains: Playwright downloads separate browser builds onto the machine running {{productName}}. They use their own browsing profile and do not share your personal browser's logins.
browserPanel.managed_host_note: These downloads land on the {{productName}} host, not on the device showing this page. A Mac viewing a Linux host gets Linux builds on that host, and installing an extension in the Mac's Chrome does not by itself let the host's CLI attach to that browser.
browserPanel.engines_help: Chromium is the default for automation. Google Chrome is a separate browser that this does not install, and WebKit is Playwright's build of Safari's engine, not your Safari app. Managed browsers are full browsers and can open visible windows. Downloaded means the files are on disk; it is not a launch test.
browserPanel.engine_unknown_reason: {{productName}} could not confirm this build from the browser cache. Downloading again is safe.
browserPanel.status_unavailable: Cannot read the browser setup status, so what is shown may be out of date.
browserPanel.failure_no_detail: The host reported no further detail.
browserPanel.reason_status_unavailable: Downloads are paused until the setup status loads again.
browserPanel.reason_checking: Checking whether the last request started a download. Downloads will be available once the host answers.
browserPanel.reason_engine_busy: {{engine}} is downloading. Other downloads will be available when it finishes.
browserPanel.reason_cli_busy: The Playwright CLI is being set up. Downloads will be available when it finishes.
browserPanel.reason_busy_generic: Another browser setup operation is running.
browserPanel.op_busy_generic: Browser setup is running on the {{productName}} host.
browserPanel.connect_explains: Use the tabs and logins of a browser you already run. This needs a Chromium-based browser, such as Chrome, with the Playwright extension installed.
browserPanel.connect_host_note: The browser and its extension must run on the {{productName}} host, where the CLI can reach them. An extension in a browser on another device does not connect to this host on its own.
browserPanel.connect_consent: An installed extension or a saved token does not mean a browser is connected.
browserPanel.desktop_title: Built-in browser in the desktop app
browserPanel.desktop_web_explains: Available in the {{productName}} desktop app. In the web dashboard, agents use Playwright instead.

connectionsPanel.title: OAuth apps for Connections
connectionsPanel.intro: Some providers refuse to register an OAuth client automatically. For each one below, follow its setup guide to register an app in the vendor console, paste the exact redirect URI shown here into that app, then enter the app's client ID and secret. Values set through environment variables override what is saved here.
connectionsPanel.none: Every provider in this install registers its own OAuth client, so there is nothing to configure here.
connectionsPanel.card_intro: Register an app in the {{provider}} developer console and enter its credentials below.
connectionsPanel.redirect_uri_help: Register exactly this value in the vendor console.
connectionsPanel.client_id_help: Public identifier of the registered app. Stored in config.json.
connectionsPanel.client_secret_required: {{provider}} requires a client secret at the token endpoint. Stored encrypted in the secrets vault and never shown again.
connectionsPanel.client_secret_optional: {{provider}} accepts a public client, so the secret is optional. Stored encrypted in the secrets vault and never shown again.
connectionsPanel.set_by_environment: Set by the environment variable {{name}}, which overrides any value saved here.
connectionsPanel.save_failed: Could not save the OAuth app
connectionsPanel.oauth_app_search_description: Client ID, client secret and redirect URI for a provider that needs a registered OAuth app
connectionsPanel.copy_failed: Could not copy to the clipboard. Select the redirect URI and copy it by hand.
connectionsPanel.remove_confirm: Remove the {{provider}} OAuth app? The client ID and the stored secret are deleted, and {{provider}} cannot connect until you enter them again.

appModels.title: Apps
appModels.description: The model each app's sessions and background agents start on.
appModels.row_hint: Inherit uses the Default Model above. A model picked for the session, the app's own pick (a Research Lab campaign, the Spec Builder default) and a model pinned on the app's agent or crew still win.

featurePreviewsTab.chat_on_a_crew_desc: Adds “New chat on crew” to the create menu, which starts a session on a remote crew — another machine you have connected under Settings > Remote Crew — and shows each connected crew’s sessions in their own group in the Sessions list. Unfinished.

intro.webhooks_summary: Another system can start your agent for you — CI, a review bot, a deploy pipeline — by sending a message with an access token you create on the Webhooks page.
intro.webhooks_where: A new Webhooks page opens from the “Open Webhooks” link that appears on this card in Settings once this is on; it stays out of the sidebar until the page is finished. Turning it off only hides the page again; tokens you created are kept.
intro.webhooks_media_page: The Webhooks page: token list on the left, the “Let an outside system wake up your agent” setup on the right.

featurePreviewsTab.decisions_desc: A small, fast model makes quick calls for {{productName}}, such as which of your skills fits your message. Pick the model below. If it is slow or does not answer, the built-in rule decides instead, so your reply is never held up.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_egress: While this is on, your messages and your skills' names and descriptions are sent over the internet to Jev. Every other kind of data has its own switch below and stays off until you turn it on.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_backend_required: The {{productName}} running this dashboard is older than this feature, so there is nothing to turn on yet. Update {{productName}} first, from Settings › Releases.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_endpoint_moved: You agreed to send to a different address than the one in the settings now, so nothing is being sent. Turn this off and on again to agree to the new address.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_points: What Jev decides while this is on:
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_config_unavailable: Could not read the settings, so this switch is not offered. Reload to try again.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_save_failed: Could not save this change. The saved setting is unchanged, so you can try again.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_tool_args: Also send tool-call arguments so Jev can flag risky calls
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_tool_args_desc: In a session that approves its own tool calls, this also sends the name and arguments of each call to Jev, which then puts a note on the ones it thinks are worth a look. Passwords and keys are replaced before anything is sent. It changes nothing about which tool calls are allowed. Off until you turn it on, even if the switch above is already on.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_compaction: Also send the conversation and tool-call inputs so Jev can score compaction
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_compaction_desc: Every time context fills up and {{productName}} compacts a session automatically, this sends that conversation and the inputs of the tool calls in it to Jev, and asks which ones would have been worth keeping. Tool OUTPUT is never sent — only how many characters it was. Passwords and keys are replaced before anything is sent. It is a measurement: the compaction happens exactly as it does now whatever Jev answers, and the answer appears as one line on the compaction notice. It is wider than sending one tool call's arguments — a whole session's conversation goes, not one call — so it is off until you turn it on, whatever else you have already agreed to.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_point_compaction_keep: Which tool calls a compaction would keep (measured only)
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_point_memory_recall: Which recalled memories reach the prompt
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_memory_text: Also send snippets of recalled memories so Jev can drop the ones that do not help
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_memory_text_desc: When the assistant asks its own memory a question, the entries closest in wording come back. This also sends each one's id and the first 200 characters of its text to Jev, which then says which ones to keep. It can only remove them — never add one, never reorder them — and if it is slow or unreachable they all come back as before. Passwords and keys are replaced before anything is sent. Off until you turn it on, even if the switch above is already on.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_scope_save_failed: Could not save “{{switch}}”. It is showing the saved value again.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_what_skills_select: Picks which one of your skills the message you just sent should load, or that none of them fits.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_what_tool_risk: Marks the tool calls in a session that approves its own as worth a second look. It never blocks one.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_what_message_steer: Decides whether a message you send into a running turn steers that turn or waits for the next one.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_what_model_route: Rates how hard a chat turn is, and that rating picks the model — only in a chat whose own model picker shows Auto (Jev).
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_api_key_desc: Kept in this dashboard's secret store on the machine that runs {{productName}}, never in config.json, and never shown again once you save it.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_bucket_label: Share of sessions Jev answers for
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_bucket_hint: Jev answers for {{percent}} of your sessions. The rest keep the rule this build ships with.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_history_label: Earlier conversation one decision may carry, in characters
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_history_desc: Earlier messages of yours and of the agent go with the question, newest first, up to this many characters. Tool output is never sent. Zero sends the message on its own, which is what the main Jev switch was agreed for, so a larger number sends more off the machine.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_judge_provider_desc: Jev sends the evidence to the address above, which this card's switch covers. The small model sends it to the model provider this machine already uses, so it needs no key and no extra agreement. Either way the judge only decides whether a wake is spent: if it cannot answer, the wake happens anyway.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_judge_lane_note: The small model is answering this one, so the switch above does not govern it. The evidence goes only to the model provider this machine already uses.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_judge_provider_auto: Automatic — Jev while its switch is on, otherwise the small model
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_judge_provider_jev: Jev — sends the evidence to the address above
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_judge_provider_llm: The small model — stays with your current provider
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_judge_model_desc: Only used when the judge above is the small model. Leave it on the judge agent's own model unless you want a cheaper one.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_judge_model_inherit: Keep the judge agent's own model
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_points_unavailable: The {{productName}} running this dashboard does not list what Jev decides yet. Update it from <0>Settings › Releases</0>.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_pointer_skills_max_triggered: How many skills a turn may inject is skills.max_triggered in ~/.kiro/crew/config.json.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_endpoint_pointer: This address is set in decisions.provider.endpoint in ~/.kiro/crew/config.json. The dashboard shows it and does not change it.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_provider_desc: Which model answers decisions. A local model runs on this machine, so nothing it is asked leaves it; {{productName}} downloads and runs it for you.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_provider_jev_detail: The reference model and the fastest, about 0.7 s per decision. Needs a TypeSafe API key, and what a decision point collects is sent to TypeSafe.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_provider_none_detail: Nothing is sent and no model runs. Every decision uses the built-in rules.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_no_model_note: No decision model is chosen. Pick one below to turn this on.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_provider_quality: About {{percent}} of Jev's accuracy, {{hard}} on hard decisions
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_provider_memory: Uses about {{peak}} of memory; recommended with {{total}} or more
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_provider_speed: About {{p50}} per decision on a CPU, up to {{p95}} on long inputs
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_provider_recommended: Recommended for this machine's {{memory}} of memory
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_provider_pending: The model marked In use keeps answering until you press Use this model.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_provider_measured: Accuracy is the number of correct answers on JevBench's 231 public items as a share of Jev's count, so it can exceed 100%; measured on a 10-core CPU with no time limit. In use, a decision that takes longer than the model's time limit is skipped and the point falls back to its built-in rule. The slowest answers are mostly the hard ones, so these figures are an upper bound for a slower model.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_provider_save_failed: Could not switch the decision model. The one in use has not changed.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_provider_blocked: Turned off by your organization's policy.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_egress_local: While this is on, your messages and your skills' names and descriptions are sent to the model server at the address below, on this machine. {{productName}} itself sends none of it over the internet. Every other kind of data has its own switch below and stays off until you turn it on.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_provider_unavailable: Could not read which decision model is configured.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_provider_memory_unavailable: Could not read this machine's memory, so no model is marked as recommended.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_custom_loopback_no_key: This address is on this machine, so no Jev API key is sent to it. A local proxy to hosted Jev must add the key itself.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_history_pointer: This is the most any one decision may carry, saved together with your agreement. What {{productName}} asks for is decisions.history_budget_chars in ~/.kiro/crew/config.json, and it never sends more than the number here.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_history_off: This takes effect once the main Jev switch is on.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_scope_is_the_ok: The switch below is the OK this needs.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_what_compaction_keep: Scores which of the session's tool calls a compaction would keep. Measured only — the compaction itself is unchanged.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_what_nudge_wake: Reads what a watching loop found since its last check and decides whether it is worth waking you for. It can only skip a wake, never add one, and a wake it cannot judge happens anyway.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_what_memory_recall: Drops the recalled memories that do not help, when the assistant asks its own memory a question. It can only remove them, never add one.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_api_key_remove_confirm: Removing the key cannot be undone — the vault does not hand a value back, so you would have to paste a new one.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_nudge_evidence: Also send what a watching loop has found so Jev can skip a turn
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_nudge_evidence_desc: A loop that checks on something every few minutes wakes the assistant every time, even when nothing changed. This sends what it is watching — the last few assistant messages from those sessions, and the state of any pull request it names — to Jev, and asks whether this round is worth waking anyone for. Jev can only wait or wake: it can never end the loop, and if it is slow or unreachable the loop wakes as it does today. Passwords and keys are replaced before anything is sent. It reads the sessions the loop watches rather than the one you are talking in.
featurePreviewsTab.layout_harness_desc: Turns on an in-development, developer-only harness for a new layout mechanism. Nothing you can see changes yet: the mechanism has no page of its own, so this exists only so it can be built and tested behind a switch.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_provider_download_note: The first time, {{productName}} downloads {{size}} of model files and about 1 GB of software, then starts the model for you.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_provider_memory_cost: While it runs, {{name}} keeps about {{peak}} of memory in use, even between decisions. Other sessions and apps get that much less: when memory runs low, {{productName}} runs fewer subagents at once and other software on this machine can slow down. Pick No model to free it.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_provider_ready: Downloaded. {{productName}} starts it when you press Use this model.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_runtime_installing: Installing the model's software. This happens once and can take a few minutes.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_runtime_starting: Starting the model. Decisions are skipped until it is ready.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_runtime_preparing_note: Decisions are skipped until it is ready. To stop, pick another model and press Use this model.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_runtime_poll_unavailable: Lost contact with the gateway; this progress may be out of date.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_runtime_running_off: Running on this machine, but nothing is sent to it while the Decisions switch above is off.
featurePreviewsTab.decisions_runtime_error: The model could not be started.
featurePreviewsTab.folder_conductor_desc: Lifts the chat that started a folder's other chats to the top of that folder: an accent bar down its left edge and a small conductor tag beside the agent name. This changes the order of the Sessions list, so the list stays as it is until you turn it on. The folder menu's chat item is always there.
featurePreviewsTab.crewmate_harness_desc: Adds an Agent harness setting to each mate's profile, so one mate can run on a different AI coding tool, such as Claude Code, with that tool's models, while the rest keep the default.
featurePreviewsTab.crew_mode_desc: Lets a chat hand tasks to a crew and track them on a Board.

kasBundleCard.toggle_description: Uses the KAS engine version this {{productName}} release was tested with, instead of the Kiro CLI. Applies to every new session on this {{productName}}, not just this device. Signs in with your Kiro account from Settings → Agent Harness. Takes effect when {{productName}} restarts.
kasBundleCard.off_note: Off: KAS uses your Kiro CLI install. On: it uses the engine this release ships with.
kasBundleCard.saved_restart_pending: Saved. {{productName}} is still running the previous engine route; it switches when you restart it: Settings → About → Restart gateway.
kasBundleCard.not_installed: KAS engine {{version}} is not installed yet.
kasBundleCard.install_failed: Could not start the KAS engine install.
kasBundleCard.save_failed: Could not save the KAS engine setting.
kasBundleCard.status_unavailable: Could not read the KAS engine status.

kiroSignInCard.title: Kiro sign-in
kiroSignInCard.signed_in_body: Agents run as this Kiro account. The access token is renewed automatically.
kiroSignInCard.expired_renews_on_next_use: The access token has expired and will be renewed the next time an agent needs it.
